belief: God is keeping me single because he is displeased with me.
origins: When we pray for a partner and nothing happens, it is tempting to wonder whether God is withholding it. If we carry guilt over our past, it is easy to link the two. Some teaching also pictures marriage as a reward for faithfulness, which leaves single people feeling they have failed a test.
teaches: Paul writes, “There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” The Lord says, “I know the plans I have for you… plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope,” and Paul calls singleness a gift, as marriage is. Scripture never presents marriage as a prize for good behavior or singleness as a punishment. Many faithful people, including Paul, were single.
self_statements: God is holding out on me.
He is punishing me for my past.
He gives spouses to people who are better than me.
I am being tested and failing.
God must be angry with me.
errors: Assuming I know God’s motive from my circumstances.
Believing marriage is a reward for good behavior.
Feeling lonely and concluding that God is angry.
Treating my situation as God’s response to my sin.
questions: What do I believe I did to deserve this?
Have I confessed it, and what does Scripture say about forgiveness?
Were there faithful single people in Scripture?
Is God’s love measured by relationship status?
What does Jeremiah 29:11 mean in a season of waiting?
How can I serve and grow today?
truth: There is no condemnation for me in Christ. God’s love for me was proven at the cross, not by my relationship status. Singleness is not a punishment, and I can trust God with my future while living fully today.
hw_truths: There is no condemnation for me.
God loved me while I was a sinner.
God’s plans are for my good.
I can trust Him while I wait.
log: Each time you think “God is displeased,” write Romans 8:1 and one sign of His love.
actions: Write why you think God is displeased.
If there is sin, confess it and receive forgiveness.
Put your gifts to use this week.
prayer: Lord, I have wondered if You are displeased with me. Thank You that there is no condemnation in Christ. Give me peace in this season, and help me serve You with joy. Amen.
hw_questions: Why do I think God is displeased?
What does Scripture say about singleness?
What can I trust God with?
name_example: Sarah can write: “There is no condemnation for me in Christ Jesus.”
